site.title: MirDB - Persistent Key-Value Store with Memcached Protocol
site.description: MirDB - A Persistent Key-Value Store with Memcached Protocol. Get the simplicity of memcached with the durability of disk-backed storage.

hero.title: MirDB
hero.tagline: Persistent Key-Value Store with Memcached Protocol
hero.description: Get the simplicity of memcached with the durability of disk-backed storage. MirDB persists your data using an efficient LSM tree architecture while maintaining full compatibility with the memcached protocol.

features.title: Memcached Protocol
features.description: Drop-in compatibility with standard memcached text protocol. Use your existing clients seamlessly.

features.title: Data Persistence
features.description: Unlike memcached, MirDB persists data to disk. No more cold cache problems after restarts.

features.title: LSM Tree Architecture
features.description: Efficient storage engine optimized for write-heavy workloads with multi-level compaction.

features.title: Rust Performance
features.description: Written in Rust for memory safety and high performance without garbage collection pauses.

comparison.intro: MirDB gives you the familiar memcached API with the durability you need for production workloads.

mirdb.description: Persists data to disk using SSTables

memcached.description: In-memory only, data lost on restart

mirdb.description: No cold cache - data survives restarts and is immediately available

memcached.description: Cold cache on every restart, requires cache warming

mirdb.description: LSM Tree with compaction, optimized for writes

memcached.description: Slab allocator, optimized for memory efficiency
No recovery, cache must be rebuilt

quickStart.code:
# Clone and build
git clone https://github.com/yetone/mirdb.git
cd mirdb
cargo build --release

# Run the server
./target/release/mirdb-server

# Connect with any memcached client
telnet localhost 12333
set mykey 0 0 5
hello
STORED
get mykey
VALUE mykey 0 5
hello
END

architecture.intro: MirDB uses an LSM (Log-Structured Merge) tree architecture, optimized for write-heavy workloads with efficient compaction.
architecture.diagramAlt: LSM Tree Architecture Diagram showing data flow from Write Request through WAL, Memtable, and SSTable levels

concepts.description: Ensures durability by logging writes before they're applied. Enables crash recovery.
Fast in-memory write buffer using a skip list data structure. Writes go here first after WAL.
Immutable on-disk files containing sorted key-value pairs. Organized in levels for efficient reads.
Background process that merges SSTables to reclaim space and maintain read performance.

implemented: Tokio-based async networking with memcached protocol
Memtable with skip list data structure
